title: PRD: Promptset Sentinel Framework and A/B Lifecycle Rules for Optimize
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket defines the PRD for a "Promptset Sentinel" evaluation framework and the A/B lifecycle ruleset used by Optimize to gate model changes. The goal is to produce a deterministic, auditable, and automatable set of requirements (prompt set design, sampling, statistical tests, signal weighting, escalation rules, and rollback triggers) so that model updates surfaced through Optimize meet product SLOs for quality, safety, latency, and cost.
background: Optimize currently runs evals using disparate prompt sets and ad-hoc thresholds. Several recent minor regressions slipped to customers because cohort sampling missed failure modes and automated gates were not strict enough for safety signals. We need a unified framework that: (1) defines how promptsets are stratified across cohorts, (2) specifies statistical tests and minimum sample sizes for A/B and canaries, (3) prescribes exact rollback triggers and severity actions, and (4) documents operational runbooks for rapid remediation.
scope: In scope: design of promptset sentinel taxonomy, sampling matrix and seeding rules, composite scoring function and signal weights, statistical test definitions and minimum N, A/B and canary lifecycle rules, automated gating logic for Optimize UI and backend, alerting & runbook templates, required dashboards and PRD artifacts. Out of scope: changes to low-level runtime batching/kernels, billing/price model, and non-Optimize product lines.
requirements: Promptset design: define primary dimensions (cohort, complexity, safety surface, domain) and require at least one promptset per critical cohort: Core, Long-context, Safety-edge, Low-resource (tokens<32), High-latency-sensitivity.
Sampling: stratified sampling with minimum per-cohort sample sizes (see Eval matrix) and deterministic seeding for reproducibility.

Composite score: produce a single weighted composite metric (0-100) combining Quality (Q), Safety (S), Latency (L), and Cost (C). Default weights: Q 0.60, S 0.25, L 0.10, C 0.05. Each submetric normalized to 0-100.

Regression thresholds: fail gate if composite score drops by >= 1.5 absolute points with p-value < 0.01 and effect size Cohen's d >= 0.2; OR if Safety pass rate decreases by >= 0.5 percentage points with p-value < 0.005.
A/B rules: require 80% statistical power, alpha=0.01 for primary composite signal. Minimum total N default 5k per variant, configurable by cohort based on historical variance.
Canary rules: phased canary sizes (1%, 5%, 25%) with increase only if no medium/high severity signals are triggered for 24h and composite delta CI contains zero.
Signal weighting and cohort bucketing: require per-customer cohort weighting mapping for enterprise customers (ability to override default weights in Dedicated/Private deployments).
Automation: gates must be enforced by backend pipelines with human-in-the-loop approval flows for medium severity but automatic block for high severity safety regressions.
Artifacts: must produce a canonical promptset spreadsheet, test harness in repo (git@github.com:redwood/optimize-evals.git), dashboard templates, and Confluence PRD linked in links.
Runbook: include triage playbook, rollback quick commands, postmortem checklist, and communication templates for affected customers.
eval_matrix: Core cohort: N>=2000 per variant; metrics: composite, quality (BLEU-like / human pass-rate surrogate), latency p50/p95, safety false positive rate.
Long-context cohort: N>=1500; metrics: context-truncation detection, quality at seq_len>=2048, memory/KV artifacts.
Safety-edge cohort (adversarial prompts): N>=5000; metrics: safety pass rate, escalation count; treated with stricter alpha=0.005.
Low-resource cohort (short prompts): N>=1000; metrics: token-efficiency, hallucination rate per 100 tokens.
Enterprise-cohort: mapping to customer traffic shape; require per-customer canary if enabled by contract.
statistical_tests: Primary test: stratified two-sided t-test on composite score with bootstrap CI for non-normal distributions. Require p<0.01 and power>=0.8 for actionable regression claims.
Safety tests: proportion z-test (or Fisher exact when counts small) for pass/fail safety flags. Defensive alpha=0.005 for safety signals.
Multiple comparisons: apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across cohorts for exploratory signals; for primary gates use per-cohort thresholds with pre-registered metrics.
Effect size: report Cohen's d and minimum detectable effect (MDE) given sample sizes; require d>=0.2 for a gate-altering regression unless safety is implicated.
Sequential testing: for canaries with rolling windows, use alpha-spending (O'Brien-Fleming) to avoid inflated Type I error.
rollout_strategy: Staged rollout: default flow is internal -> 1% canary -> 5% canary -> 25% -> full. Each stage requires 24h observation window and no gateway violations to progress.
Canary monitoring: automated dashboards showing composite and submetrics per cohort; thresholds visualized and annotated with decision labels (OK, Watch, Fail).
Human gate: PM/ENG/RESEARCH sign-off required to proceed from 25%->100% for major model-version bumps or when any customer-facing change is present.
Fallback policies: automatic seamless fallback to previous model variant on automatic rollback; data retention of failure-run traces for postmortem.
rollback_triggers: Immediate automatic rollback: any high-severity safety regression (safety pass rate drop >= 0.5 pp AND p<0.005) OR a reproducible toxic generation discovered in >=0.1% of samples in safety-edge cohort.
Escalated rollback (manual but urgent): composite score drop >= 3.0 points with p<0.01 across Core cohort or latency p95 increase > 50% for Core/Long cohorts.

Soft stop & investigation: composite drop between 1.5 and 3.0 points OR marginal safety regression (0.2-0.5 pp) triggers an immediate halt on further ramp and a 48h investigation window with embargoed traffic hold on new enterprise canaries.
No rollback: small fluctuations below thresholds (composite <1.5 points) documented and monitored; requires action only if persistent for 7 days or trending downwards in slope > 0.25 points/day.
Manual override: on-call PL may temporarily pause rollout for operational incidents (latency, infra) even if model gates pass; follow-up postmortem required.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical promptset created, reviewed by Research and Safety, stored in the Optimize promptset registry with versioning and changelog.
Evaluation harness implemented and runnable end-to-end from pipeline with a single CI job; sample seeding deterministic across runs.
Dashboards: Composite and per-cohort dashboards live in Grafana with alerting rules matching rollback_triggers and documented runbook links.
Automatic gating: backend blocks rollout to next stage when any gate fails; tests cover gating logic and threshold config is feature-flagged.
Documentation: PRD, runbook, and statistical test specification published in Confluence; template emails and customer comms prepared.
DRY-RUN: one planned canary run with synthetic delta to validate detection and rollback (postmortem required) prior to production adoption.
